generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the work you are already doing. As you near the end of a degree, you are expected to direct your own study, to recognise the capital that study is building, and to say clearly what you have become. The students who do this on purpose are the ones who can make a strong case for themselves, rather than leaving their development unspoken. Treat what follows as being about your own degree and your own next step, not about study in the abstract.

The same moves carry into professional life. Applications, interviews and appraisals all ask you to regulate your own work, show the capital you bring, and articulate your development with evidence. Learning to do that now is a habit you keep long after you graduate.
